High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
1. This is applicants first application under Section 438 of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 for grant of anticipatory bail, as they are apprehending their arrest in connection with Crime No.178/2024 registered at Police Station Varla, District Badwani (MP) for offence punishable under Section 376,
376(d), 294, 342 r/w 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
2. Allegations against the applicants are that they were also involved in the aforesaid case wherein prosecutrix was subjected to rape by the co-accused Kalu Singh while Gulab Singh hold her hands.
It is alleged against the applicants that they were standing outside the house and guarding the door.

3. Counsel for the applicants has submitted that the applicants have been falsely implicated in the case for the reason that the mother of applicant No.1 who happens to be a student of B.Sc. had lodged an FIR at crime No.152/2024 on 26/04/2024 under Section 376 of IPC against the father of the prosecutrix and the other accused persons and as a counter blast, the present FIR has been lodged by the prosecutrix involving four persons of the same family.
Counsel 2 MCRC-29028-2024 has submitted that admittedly, the FIR has been lodged after a delay of 12 hours and there is no injury reflected in the MLC also.
Thus, it is submitted that the application be allowed as no purpose would be served to arrest the applicants in a false case.
Counsel has also drawn the attention of this Court to the FIR lodged by the mother of applicant No.1 against father of the prosecutrix, which is also filed on record.

It is also submitted that applicant No.2 Nansingh happens to be the son of co-accused Gulab Singh, thus, it is submitted that it is also improbable that father would commit an offence of rape and the son would protect his father standing outside.
Hence, it is submitted that the application be allowed and the applicants be released on anticipatory bail.

sentences.text: Counsel for the respondent / State, on the other hand, has opposed the prayer and it is submitted that no case for anticipatory bail is made out as there is a clear statement given by prosecutrix and her sister-in-law under Section 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C., thus it is not a case of grant of anticipatory bail, however, it is not denied that in the MLC, there is no injury suffered by the prosecutrix.

5. On due consideration of the rival submissions and perusal of the case diary as also the documents filed on record, this Court is of the considered opinion that the applicants have made out a case for grant of anticipatory bail as under the facts and circumstances of the case, when the father of the accused is already an accused in a case wherein it is alleged that the mother of applicant No.1 was ravished by him, in such circumstances, the custodial interrogation of the applicants is not necessary in the present case.
6. Accordingly, this application is allowed.

It is directed that in the event of arrest, applicant shall be released on bail, upon his executing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- (rupees twenty five thousand only) and furnishing one 3 MCRC-29028-2024 solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer (Investigating Officer).

However, it is made clear that subsequently if the DNA report is found to be positive, in that case, this order shall stand cancelled automatically.
7.
The applicant shall make himself available for interrogation by a Police Officer, as and when required.
He shall further abide by the other conditions enumerated in Sub Section (2) of Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
Certified copy as per rules.
